intro.title: Restaurant Menu List
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a restaurant menu list app that displays food items with their names, descriptions, and prices. You'll learn how to create and manage data arrays in TypeScript to store menu information. The main technologies involved are Ionic components for the UI, Angular for data binding, and TypeScript for type-safe data structures. By the end, you'll have a functional menu list that dynamically displays restaurant items in a clean, scrollable interface.
intro.usecase: This restaurant menu pattern is used in countless food delivery apps like Uber Eats, DoorDash, and Grubhub, where users browse categorized menus with item details and prices. It's also essential for restaurant POS systems where staff need to view available menu items during order taking. Similar list-category interfaces appear in e-commerce product catalogs, hotel service menus, and digital storefronts where items are organized into logical groups for easy navigation and selection.
